The transcription and the second transcription are both OCR passes over this print and flatten the Greek the same way, so neither can settle it. The leaf was drawn 4 time(s) over 2 model(s) (google/gemini-2.5-flash, anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5); the 2 draw(s) that read these characters were google/gemini-2.5-flash — ONE instrument repeated, not two, so this reading rests on that model alone. (decided by the page image itself.) ONE INSTRUMENT'S READING: these letters rest on ONE reader, google/gemini-2.5-flash — no second reader's own draws corroborate them. The rule is merged with that fact stated, the review flag stands on it, and the rule is listed in the edition's review worklist.THE READING THIS RULE SERVED WAS FABRICATED. It read “ορουμ and θεῖα”, and NEITHER WORD ENDS IN ω WHILE THE PRINT’S OWN SENTENCE ON THAT LINE SAYS THE LETTER DISCUSSED “is here an ω” — and the OCR renders the print’s standalone ω in that very clause as “m” (“which letter is here an m”), so the rule made the same μ/ω misdecode twice. The print reads “from ὀρούω and θείω, according to the Attic custom of adding a letter at the end of a word, which letter is here an ω”, per the human-proofread word-level transcription of this print (Project Gutenberg ebook 77393 / 78800, Distributed Proofreaders) and a BLIND read of the page image (the candidate text never shown to the model, google/gemini-2.5-flash, the whole page and an archive crop of the same line) — the human-proofread transcription reads “from ορουω and θειω”, and the blind read of a crop of that line on archive leaf v2-n732 gives “ὀρούω and θείω”. Both are real Greek verbs of rushing, which is the derivation the sentence states. THE REVIEW FLAG IS RESTORED. It was cleared at 1.0.4 on a witness verdict that cannot see Greek: the witness locator’s token stream is ASCII letters and digits ONLY, so for a transliteration rule its “the witness carries the rule’s whole `after` reading” test is decided on the English AROUND the Greek and the Greek the rule exists to supply is never compared.
